examples.en: I was so tired that I fell asleep as soon as I lay down on the bedding.

examples.ko: 손님이 오기 전에 이부자리를 깔아 놓았어요.
examples.en: I laid out the bedding before the guest arrived.
When I get up in the morning, I fold up my bedding right away.
The bedding was damp, so I hung it out in the sun.

examples.ko: 여행 가방에 이부자리까지 넣을 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't fit bedding into my travel bag too.
The bedding spread on the warmest part of the floor is really warm.

explain: '이불'은 덮는 것만 가리키지만 '이부자리'는 요와 이불, 보통 베개까지 잠자리 한 벌을 말해요. '깔다', '펴다', '개다'와 함께 자주 써요. 침대보다는 바닥에 까는 잠자리가 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '이불' is only the cover you put over yourself, while '이부자리' means the whole set: mattress pad, quilt and usually the pillow. It is often used with '깔다', '펴다' and '개다'. It fits floor bedding better than a bed.

examples.en: The board of directors unanimously elected a new CEO.

examples.ko: 이사회가 표결 없이 박수로 안건을 통과시켰어요.
examples.en: The board passed the item by applause without a vote.

examples.ko: 이사회는 다음 주 금요일에 열릴 예정이에요.
examples.en: The board meeting is scheduled for next Friday.
At this board meeting, they approved the new budget.
The president decided to follow the board's decision.
I went to work early in the morning to attend the board meeting.

explain: 회사나 학교, 단체에서 큰 결정을 내리는 모임이라 보통 '회의'보다 무게가 있어요. '이사회를 열다', '이사회에서 의결하다'처럼 쓰고, 주주들의 모임은 '주주총회'라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is the body that makes major decisions in a company, school or organization, so it feels weightier than a plain '회의' (meeting). Typical uses are '이사회를 열다' and '이사회에서 의결하다'. A shareholders' meeting is called '주주총회' instead.

examples.en: I chatted happily with friends I hadn't seen in a long time.
Lively talk went on late into the night at Grandma's house.

examples.ko: 커피 한 잔 놓고 이야기꽃을 피워 볼까요?
examples.en: Shall we sit down with a coffee and have a good chat?
When the family gets together, the conversation never stops.
At the alumni reunion, the talk bloomed all night long.
We chatted away for the whole lunch break.

explain: 대부분 '이야기꽃을 피우다'로 쓰고, 이야기가 즐겁게 이어지는 분위기를 꽃에 빗댄 말이에요. 진지한 토론이나 말다툼에는 어울리지 않아요. '이야기꽃이 피다'처럼 '피다'도 함께 써요.

phrases.example: 오랜만에 만난 친구와 밤새 이야기꽃을 피웠어요.
phrases.en: I talked happily all night with a friend I hadn't seen in ages.
phrases.nuance_ko: 즐겁고 활발하게 이야기가 오가는 모습을 꽃이 피는 것에 빗대요. 다투거나 진지하게 토론할 때는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: It likens a cheerful, lively conversation to flowers blooming. It is not used for arguments or serious debates.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '이야기꽃을 피우다', comparing a pleasant, flowing conversation to blooming flowers. It does not suit serious debates or arguments. You can also say '이야기꽃이 피다'.

examples.en: My grandfather is a well-known storyteller in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 타고난 이야기꾼이라 말이 재미있어요.
examples.en: That friend is a born storyteller, so everything they say is fun.
In the old days, storytellers often showed up at the market.
The children listened closely to the storyteller's voice.

examples.ko: 저는 이야기꾼이 아니라서 농담을 잘 못해요.
examples.en: I'm not much of a storyteller, so I'm bad at telling jokes.
Try telling it vividly, like a storyteller.

explain: '-꾼'이 붙은 '일꾼', '장사꾼'처럼 어떤 일을 잘하거나 즐겨 하는 사람을 말해요. 이야기를 재미있게 잘하는 사람에게 칭찬으로 쓰기도 해요. 같은 느낌으로 '입담이 좋다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Like '일꾼' and '장사꾼', the '-꾼' ending marks someone who does something often or well. It can be a compliment for someone who tells stories in an entertaining way. '입담이 좋다' describes a similar skill.

examples.ko: 이왕에 가는 김에 편지도 부쳐 주세요.
examples.en: Since you're going anyway, please mail the letter too.
Now that we've started, let's see it through.

examples.ko: 이왕에 사 먹을 거면 좋은 걸로 사요.
examples.en: If you're going to buy it anyway, get a good one.
Since we're already on Jeju, let's climb Hallasan too.
We're late already, so let's take it slow today.
If it has to be done anyway, let's do it happily.

explain: 이미 그렇게 된 김에, 어차피 할 거라면 하는 느낌이라서 '-ㄴ 김에', '-ㄹ 거면'과 자주 어울려요. 그냥 '이왕'이라고 해도 되고, '기왕에'라고도 말해요. '이왕이면'은 선택할 때 기왕 하는 거 좋은 쪽으로 하자고 할 때 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of 'since it's already like this' or 'if we're doing it anyway', so it pairs well with '-ㄴ 김에' and '-ㄹ 거면'. You can also say just '이왕' or '기왕에'. '이왕이면' is used when choosing the better option while you're at it.

examples.ko: 아기가 이유식을 잘 먹어서 정말 다행이에요.
examples.en: I'm so relieved that the baby eats baby food well.

examples.ko: 아기에게 이유식을 먹이는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Feeding the baby weaning food takes a long time.

examples.ko: 저는 주말마다 이유식 재료를 사러 마트에 가요.
examples.en: Every weekend I go to the supermarket to buy ingredients for baby food.

examples.ko: 요즘은 시판 이유식도 종류가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: These days there are many kinds of store-bought baby food too.

examples.ko: 이유식을 먹일 때마다 아기가 자꾸 뱉어요.
examples.en: Every time I feed the baby solids, the baby keeps spitting them out.
At first, we start with baby food made from rice.

explain: 젖이나 분유만 먹던 아기가 밥으로 넘어가는 중간 단계의 음식이라 육아 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '이유식을 만들다', '이유식을 먹이다'처럼 쓰고, 그다음 단계 음식은 '유아식'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the in-between food for a baby moving from milk or formula to regular meals, so it comes up a lot in parenting talk. It goes with '이유식을 만들다' and '이유식을 먹이다'. The next stage of food is called '유아식'.

examples.ko: 새 책상의 이음새가 헐거워서 자꾸 흔들려요.
examples.en: The joints of the new desk are loose, so it keeps wobbling.
The seam of the wallpaper has visibly come apart.
Water is leaking from the pipe joint.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 이음새가 깔끔해서 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like this piece of clothing because its seams are neat.
Please apply glue to the joint.

examples.ko: 이음새가 보이지 않게 잘 붙여 주세요.
examples.en: Please attach it well so the seam doesn't show.

explain: '이음매'라고도 하고 쓰임이 거의 같아요. 가구, 배관, 옷, 벽지처럼 두 부분을 붙인 자리를 말할 때 써요. '벌어지다', '헐겁다', '새다'처럼 문제가 생겼을 때 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is also said as '이음매' and is used in nearly the same way. It refers to the spot where two parts are joined, in furniture, pipes, clothes or wallpaper. It often appears with '벌어지다', '헐겁다' and '새다' when something goes wrong.

examples.en: Yesterday I listened to a piano and violin duet.
The two players' duet was truly beautiful.
I'm practicing a guitar duet with my younger sibling.
Applause poured in after the duet performance ended.
I decided to perform as a duet with my friend.

examples.ko: 이중주는 두 사람이 호흡을 맞추는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: In a duet, it's important for the two players to be in sync.

explain: 악기 두 개나 두 사람이 함께하는 연주에 써요. 노래를 둘이 부르는 건 '이중창'이라고 구분해요. 셋이 연주하면 '삼중주'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is for a piece played by two instruments or two players. Two people singing together is called '이중창' instead. A piece for three players is a '삼중주'.

examples.ko: 이즈음에는 날씨가 하루에도 몇 번씩 변해요.
examples.en: These days the weather changes several times a day.
We first met around this time last year.
Lately I've been feeling much more tired.
Every year around this time, the autumn leaves turn beautifully.
Lately my friends all seem busy.
Kids these days start using smartphones early.

explain: '요즘'과 비슷하지만 말투가 조금 글 같고, '작년 이즈음'처럼 어느 때쯤을 가리킬 때도 써요. 해마다 돌아오는 같은 시기를 말할 때는 '이맘때'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is close to '요즘' but sounds a little more literary, and it can point to a specific time of year, as in '작년 이즈음'. For the same time each year, people also say '이맘때'.

examples.en: Computers process all information in binary.
In the binary system, only the digits 0 and 1 are used.
We learned binary calculation in class.
Converting decimal into binary is difficult.

examples.ko: 이진법은 컴퓨터를 공부할 때 꼭 나와요.
examples.en: Binary always comes up when you study computers.
My younger sibling said their age in binary, and I laughed.

explain: 우리가 평소 쓰는 '십진법'과 짝으로 배우는 말이에요. 방법이나 체계를 말하고, 그 방법으로 나타낸 수는 '이진수'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is learned as a pair with '십진법', the decimal system we normally use. It refers to the system itself, while a number written in that system is called '이진수'.

examples.en: Let's stop here for today and take a rest.
Sir, you can stop around here.

examples.ko: 이야기는 이쯤 해 두고 밥 먹어요.
examples.en: Let's leave the talk at that and eat.

examples.ko: 물이 이쯤 차면 불을 꺼 주세요.
examples.en: When the water fills up to about here, please turn off the heat.
I think this is enough of an explanation.
By this point, I start wanting to give up.

explain: 정도, 장소, 때를 모두 가리킬 수 있어서 '이쯤에서 그만하자', '이쯤 하면 충분해요'처럼 마무리할 때 자주 써요. 말하는 사람에게 가까우면 '이쯤', 듣는 사람 쪽이면 '그쯤', 멀면 '저쯤'을 써요. 비슷한 말로 '이 정도'가 있어요.
explain_en: It can refer to degree, place or time, and is often used to wrap things up, as in '이쯤에서 그만하자'. Use '이쯤' for what is near the speaker, '그쯤' for near the listener, and '저쯤' for far away. '이 정도' is a similar expression.

examples.en: When autumn came, the leaves turned yellow.
One leaf fell from the branch.

examples.ko: 우리 집 화분 이파리에 먼지가 쌓였어요.
examples.en: Dust has settled on the leaves of my potted plant.
Bugs ate up all the leaves.

examples.ko: 상추 이파리를 크게 펴서 쌈을 싸요.
examples.en: I spread out a big lettuce leaf and make a wrap.
If the leaves wilt, give it more water.

explain: '잎'과 같은 대상을 말하지만 말할 때 더 편하고 정겹게 들려요. 나무뿐 아니라 풀이나 채소의 잎에도 써요. '이파리가 무성하다', '이파리가 시들다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the same thing as '잎' but sounds more casual and familiar in speech. It is used for the leaves of trees, grasses and vegetables alike. Common phrases are '이파리가 무성하다' and '이파리가 시들다'.

examples.en: My mom is very understanding.
I'm lucky to have met such an understanding teacher.
Please be a little more understanding toward your friend.
Thanks to my roommate's understanding, I live comfortably.
If people lack understanding of each other, they fight easily.

examples.ko: 부부 사이에는 서로에 대한 이해심이 필요해요.
examples.en: Between spouses, mutual understanding is needed.

explain: '이해심이 깊다/많다/부족하다'처럼 남의 사정을 헤아리고 받아들이는 마음을 말해요. 내용을 알아듣는 능력인 '이해력'과 달라요. 성격을 칭찬할 때 '이해심이 많은 사람'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used as '이해심이 깊다/많다/부족하다' for the heart that considers and accepts other people's situations. It differs from '이해력', the ability to grasp content. To praise someone's character, say '이해심이 많은 사람'.

en: living national treasure; holder of intangible cultural heritage

examples.en: That person is a living cultural treasure in traditional dance.

examples.ko: 인간문화재가 직접 도자기를 만드는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a living national treasure make pottery by hand.
I want to learn pansori from a living national treasure.
A teacher who is a living national treasure lives in our town.
It takes a long time to be designated a living national treasure.
I watched a living national treasure's performance at the museum.

explain: 전통 기술이나 예능을 이어 가는 '사람'을 가리키고, 건물이나 물건은 그냥 '문화재'라고 해요. 공식 명칭은 '국가무형문화재 보유자'지만 일상에서는 '인간문화재'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who carries on a traditional craft or performing art, while buildings and objects are simply '문화재'. The official title is '국가무형문화재 보유자', but in daily talk people often say '인간문화재'.

examples.en: The bank clerk told me to bring my registered seal.

examples.ko: 집을 살 때 인감도장이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: You absolutely need a registered seal when buying a house.
I lost my registered seal, so I had a new one made.
You must not lend your registered seal to just anyone.
I went to the community center and registered my seal.
Please stamp your registered seal on this document.

explain: 미리 관청에 등록해 두고 중요한 계약이나 서류에 쓰는 도장이라 평소에 쓰는 '막도장'과 달라요. 줄여서 '인감'이라고도 하고, 도장이 맞는지 증명하는 서류는 '인감증명서'예요.
explain_en: This is a seal registered in advance with the authorities and used for important contracts and documents, unlike an everyday '막도장'. It is often shortened to '인감', and the document proving it is genuine is the '인감증명서'.

examples.en: Raising a child takes a lot of patience.
In a marathon, endurance matters as much as physical strength.
After waiting so long, my patience ran out.

examples.ko: 그는 인내력이 강해서 쉽게 포기하지 않아요.
examples.en: He has strong endurance and doesn't give up easily.
To build your perseverance, start with small goals.

examples.ko: 동생은 인내력이 약해서 공부를 금방 그만둬요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has little endurance and quits studying quickly.

explain: '참을성'과 비슷하지만 '인내력'은 조금 더 격식 있고, 참고 견디는 힘이라는 능력 느낌이 있어요. '인내력이 강하다/약하다/필요하다'처럼 써요. 마음가짐을 말할 때는 '인내심'을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '참을성' but a bit more formal, with a feel of an ability or strength to endure. You say '인내력이 강하다/약하다/필요하다'. When talking about mindset, '인내심' is also used.

examples.en: I hear that every restaurant is badly short of staff these days.

examples.ko: 그 공장은 인력난 때문에 문을 닫을 뻔했어요.
examples.en: That factory almost closed because of a labor shortage.

examples.ko: 농촌은 젊은 사람이 없어서 인력난을 겪어요.
examples.en: Rural areas suffer from labor shortages because there are no young people.
If the labor shortage continues, wages sometimes rise.

examples.ko: 병원이 인력난을 해결하려고 직원을 더 뽑아요.
examples.en: The hospital is hiring more staff to solve its manpower shortage.
A sudden staff shortage came up, so everyone worked overtime.

explain: '-난'은 구하기 어렵다는 뜻을 더하는 말로 '구인난', '취업난'과 같은 방식이에요. 일할 사람이 모자란 회사나 업계 입장에서 쓰고, 일상에서는 '일손이 부족하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-난' adds the sense of difficulty or shortage, as in '구인난' and '취업난'. It is used from the viewpoint of a company or industry short of workers, and in daily talk people also say '일손이 부족하다'.

en: the good fortune of knowing helpful people

examples.ko: 저는 인복이 많아서 좋은 사람들을 만났어요.
examples.en: I'm lucky with people, so I've met good ones.

examples.ko: 인복이 없는지 늘 사람 때문에 힘들어요.
examples.en: Maybe I'm unlucky with people; I always struggle because of others.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 인복을 타고난 것 같아요.
examples.en: That person seems born with good luck in people.

examples.ko: 인복 많은 친구라서 어디서나 도움을 받아요.
examples.en: My friend is lucky with people, so they get help everywhere.
Meeting such a good senior, you're lucky with people.
I think even luck with people comes only with effort.

explain: '인복이 많다/없다'처럼 써서 주변에 도와주고 잘해 주는 사람이 많은 운을 말해요. '재복', '처복'처럼 '-복'이 붙은 말들과 같은 방식이에요. 좋은 사람을 만난 걸 부러워하거나 칭찬할 때 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Used as '인복이 많다/없다', it refers to the luck of having many people around who help and treat you well. It is built like other '-복' words such as '재복' and '처복'. People say it when envying or praising someone for meeting good people.

en: courteousness in greetings; politeness in greetings

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 인사성이 밝아서 칭찬을 받아요.
examples.en: My son is good at greeting people, so he gets praised.
An employee who doesn't greet people is a bit disappointing.
The neighbors say he's a child with good manners in greeting.
If you greet people well, you're liked everywhere.

examples.ko: 그 가게 사장님은 인사성이 참 좋으세요.
examples.en: The owner of that shop is really good about greeting customers.

examples.ko: 인사성을 기르려면 먼저 웃으며 인사해 보세요.
examples.en: To get in the habit of greeting people, try smiling and saying hello first.

explain: 인사를 잘하는 성격이나 태도를 말해서 '인사성이 밝다/바르다/좋다/없다'처럼 써요. 칭찬할 때 '예의 바르다'보다 인사하는 모습에 초점을 둬요. 어린아이나 직원, 이웃을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes a disposition of greeting people well, used as '인사성이 밝다/바르다/좋다/없다'. Compared with '예의 바르다', it focuses specifically on how someone greets others. It often comes up when talking about children, employees or neighbors.

en: path of life; course of life; journey of life

examples.en: A person's life path is long and far, like a marathon.

examples.ko: 부모님은 제 인생길을 늘 응원해 주세요.
examples.en: My parents always support my path in life.
Even on a rough road of life, my friend was by my side.
The road of life has both uphills and downhills.

examples.ko: 저는 이제 새로운 인생길을 걷기 시작했어요.
examples.en: I have now started walking a new path in life.

examples.ko: 그 선택은 제 인생길을 완전히 바꿔 놓았어요.
examples.en: That choice completely changed the course of my life.

explain: 인생을 걸어가는 길에 빗댄 말이라 노래, 편지, 연설에서 자주 나와요. '인생길을 걷다', '험한 인생길'처럼 말하고, 평소 대화에서는 그냥 '인생'이라고 해도 충분해요.
explain_en: It pictures life as a road you walk, so it shows up often in songs, letters and speeches. Typical uses are '인생길을 걷다' and '험한 인생길'. In ordinary conversation, plain '인생' is usually enough.

examples.ko: 제 인생철학은 하루하루 최선을 다하는 거예요.
examples.en: My philosophy of life is to do my best every single day.
I want to learn my grandfather's philosophy of life.

examples.ko: 그 책에는 작가의 인생철학이 잘 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: The author's philosophy of life comes through well in that book.

examples.ko: 인생철학이 뚜렷한 사람은 쉽게 흔들리지 않아요.
examples.en: People with a clear philosophy of life aren't easily shaken.

examples.ko: 면접에서 자신의 인생철학을 말해 보라고 했어요.
examples.en: In the interview, they asked me to talk about my philosophy of life.
My philosophy of life changed while I was traveling.

explain: 학문으로서의 철학이 아니라 개인이 삶에서 지키는 생각이나 원칙을 말해요. '가치관'과 비슷하지만 '인생철학'은 한마디로 말할 수 있는 신조 같은 느낌이 있어요. '제 인생철학은 ~예요'처럼 자기소개나 인터뷰에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is not philosophy as an academic field but the personal ideas or principles a person lives by. It is close to '가치관', though '인생철학' feels more like a motto you can sum up in one line. You often hear '제 인생철학은 ~예요' in introductions and interviews.

examples.en: That coach makes us practice mercilessly.

examples.ko: 인정사정없이 비가 쏟아져서 옷이 다 젖었어요.
examples.en: The rain poured down relentlessly and soaked my clothes.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 인정사정없이 공격해서 우리가 졌어요.
examples.en: The other team attacked without mercy, and we lost.
Some customers try to bargain the price down ruthlessly.
The boss scolded the employee who made a mistake without mercy.

examples.ko: 인정사정없이 달려드는 모기 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: Mosquitoes kept attacking relentlessly, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: 사람의 인정이나 사정을 하나도 봐주지 않는다는 느낌이 강해서 대개 부정적으로 써요. 사람뿐 아니라 비나 추위, 모기처럼 봐주지 않고 몰아치는 것에도 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '가차 없이'가 있는데 더 딱딱해요.
explain_en: It strongly implies showing no consideration for feelings or circumstances, so it is usually negative. It can describe people but also relentless things like rain, cold or mosquitoes. '가차 없이' is a similar but stiffer expression.

examples.en: I was so nervous that sweat formed above my upper lip.
Looking in the mirror, I saw something had come up above my lip.
After drinking milk, I had a white mark above my lip.
I caught a cold, and the skin under my nose got red and sore.
The pimple above my lip bothers me.
I nicked the skin above my lip while shaving.

explain: 코와 윗입술 사이에 살짝 들어간 부분을 가리키는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '코 밑'이라고 말하기도 해요. 땀이 나거나 감기 때문에 헐었을 때처럼 몸 상태를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It names the small groove between the nose and the upper lip. In daily talk people sometimes just say '코 밑'. It often comes up when describing how your body feels, such as sweating there or having it chapped from a cold.

examples.ko: 급한 일이 생겨서 인터폰으로 경비실에 연락했어요.
examples.en: Something urgent came up, so I contacted the guard office by intercom.

examples.ko: 초인종 대신 인터폰이 울려서 나가 봤어요.
examples.en: The intercom rang instead of the doorbell, so I went to check.
The delivery driver appeared on the intercom screen.

examples.ko: 우리 아파트 인터폰이 고장 나서 수리를 신청했어요.
examples.en: The intercom in our apartment broke, so I requested a repair.

examples.ko: 경비 아저씨가 손님이 왔다고 인터폰으로 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The security guard told me by intercom that a visitor had arrived.
I answered the intercom, but there was no voice.

explain: 아파트 현관, 경비실, 집 안끼리 연결해서 말하는 장치라 한국 아파트 생활에서 자주 나와요. '인터폰이 울리다', '인터폰을 받다'처럼 말해요. 영어로는 interphone보다 intercom이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: This is the device that connects an apartment's entrance, the guard office and the rooms inside, so it comes up a lot in Korean apartment life. People say '인터폰이 울리다' and '인터폰을 받다'. In English, 'intercom' sounds more natural than 'interphone'.

en: all the family and relatives; kinsfolk

examples.ko: 명절에는 일가친척이 모두 할머니 댁에 모여요.
examples.en: On holidays, all our relatives gather at Grandma's house.
We invited all our relatives to our wedding.

examples.ko: 일가친척 중에 의사는 한 명도 없어요.
examples.en: There isn't a single doctor among our relatives.

examples.ko: 저는 일가친척이 많지 않아서 명절이 조용해요.
examples.en: I don't have many relatives, so holidays are quiet.
I was busy greeting all the relatives.
Many of our relatives live in this neighborhood.

explain: 가까운 친척뿐 아니라 먼 친척까지 온 집안 사람들을 한꺼번에 가리키는 느낌이에요. 가까운 사이를 말할 때는 보통 그냥 '친척'이라고 해요. 명절, 결혼식, 장례식처럼 집안 모임 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It conveys the whole extended family at once, close and distant relatives together. When talking about a specific close relative, people usually say plain '친척'. It often appears when discussing family gatherings such as holidays, weddings and funerals.

examples.ko: 일개미는 먹이를 쉬지 않고 부지런히 날라요.
examples.en: Worker ants carry food diligently without rest.
Worker ants walk in a line in front of the anthill.
Worker ants swarmed over the sugar.

examples.ko: 아이가 일개미 행렬을 한참 동안 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The child watched a line of worker ants for a long time.

examples.ko: 일개미 한 마리가 제 발등을 기어갔어요.
examples.en: A worker ant crawled across the top of my foot.

examples.ko: 여왕개미는 알을 낳고 일개미는 먹이를 구해요.
examples.en: The queen ant lays eggs, and worker ants gather food.

explain: 개미 집단에서 먹이를 구하고 집을 짓는 개미를 말하고, 알을 낳는 '여왕개미'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 비유로는 쉬지 않고 일만 하는 사람을 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 시키는 일만 하니 일개미 같아요.
phrases.en: All day I only do what I'm told, so I feel like a worker ant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 쉬지 않고 일하지만 눈에 띄지 않는 사람이 자기 처지를 말할 때 써요. 조금 자조적인 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by someone who works nonstop at a job without being noticed, describing their own situation. It has a slightly self-mocking tone.

explain_en: This is the ant that gathers food and builds the nest, often mentioned alongside the egg-laying '여왕개미' (queen ant). Figuratively it points to a person who does nothing but work.

examples.en: It's hard to find laborers during the farming season.

examples.ko: 일꾼들이 점심을 먹고 다시 일을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The workers ate lunch and went back to work.

examples.ko: 그 집 아들은 일 잘하는 일꾼이에요.
examples.en: That family's son is a hard worker.

examples.ko: 이사하는 날 일꾼 세 명이 와 줬어요.
examples.en: Three workers came to help on moving day.
I'm glad the newly hired worker is diligent.
Every vacation I worked as a laborer at a construction site.

explain: 주로 농사, 공사처럼 몸으로 하는 일을 하는 사람에게 써서 사무실 직원에게는 어울리지 않아요. '일 잘하는 일꾼'처럼 칭찬으로도 쓰고, 정치인이 '국민의 일꾼'이라고 자신을 낮추어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is mainly for people doing physical work such as farming or construction, so it doesn't suit office staff. It can be praise, as in '일 잘하는 일꾼', and politicians sometimes humbly call themselves '국민의 일꾼' (the people's servant).

examples.en: The results of this study are hard to generalize.
If the sample is small, there are limits to generalization.
Hasty generalization creates misunderstandings.
With smartphones becoming commonplace, daily life has changed a lot.
Be careful not to over-generalize.
In my presentation, the problem of generalization was pointed out.

explain: 한 가지 경험을 전체로 넓혀 말하는 뜻으로 '그건 지나친 일반화예요'처럼 대화에서도 많이 말해요. 어떤 것이 널리 퍼져 보편적이 되었다는 뜻으로도 써요. 행동으로 말할 때는 '일반화하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It covers extending one experience to everything, and is common in conversation as in '그건 지나친 일반화예요'. It can also mean something becoming widespread and commonplace. For the action, use the verb '일반화하다'.

examples.ko: 몇 사람 의견으로 전체를 일반화하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't generalize about everyone from a few people's opinions.

examples.ko: 표본이 너무 작으면 결과를 일반화하기 어려워요.
examples.en: If the sample is too small, it's hard to generalize the results.

examples.ko: 한국 사람은 다 그렇다고 일반화하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't generalize and say all Koreans are like that.

examples.ko: 교수님이 이 이론을 다른 분야에도 일반화해 보자고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The professor suggested we try generalizing this theory to other fields too.

examples.ko: 한 번 실패한 걸 일반화해서 늘 불안해해요.
examples.en: He overgeneralizes from one failure and is always anxious.

examples.ko: 사례가 많아야 결론을 일반화할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can generalize a conclusion only when there are many cases.

explain: '일반화하지 마세요', '일반화하면 안 돼요'처럼 부정적인 말과 함께 자주 나와요. 한두 번 본 걸로 전부 그렇다고 말하는 것을 가리키기 때문이에요. 널리 퍼지게 한다는 뜻도 있지만 그때는 '일반화되다'가 더 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: It often appears with negatives, as in '일반화하지 마세요' and '일반화하면 안 돼요', pointing to claiming something is true of all based on one or two cases. It can also mean making something widespread, but then the passive '일반화되다' is more common.

examples.ko: 더운 날 밖에서 오래 놀다가 일사병에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I got sunstroke from playing outside too long on a hot day.

examples.ko: 일사병을 막으려면 모자를 쓰고 물을 자주 마시세요.
examples.en: To prevent sunstroke, wear a hat and drink water often.
There was a student who collapsed from sunstroke on the field.

examples.ko: 일사병 증상이 있으면 그늘에서 쉬어야 해요.
examples.en: If you have symptoms of sunstroke, you should rest in the shade.

examples.ko: 뙤약볕 아래서 일하면 일사병이 생기기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Working under the scorching sun makes sunstroke easy to get.
You have to watch out for sunstroke at summer festivals.

explain: 강한 햇볕을 오래 받아서 생기는 병이에요. 비슷한 '열사병'은 몸의 열이 너무 올라가 더 위험할 때 말해요. 일상에서는 '더위를 먹다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: This is the illness caused by long exposure to strong sunlight. The similar '열사병' refers to the body overheating, which is more dangerous. In daily talk people often say '더위를 먹다' as well.

examples.en: That athlete is the world's acknowledged number one.
He is called the top figure in the field of cooking.
To become number one, you have to practice every day.
Minsu is the top math student in our class.
They say that person is the best in this field.

examples.ko: 일인자의 자리를 지키는 건 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Staying at the top spot is not easy.

explain: 어떤 분야에서 가장 뛰어난 사람을 말해서 '최고'나 '1등'과 비슷하지만 사람에게만 써요. 조직에서 가장 높은 사람을 가리킬 때도 있고, 그 아래 사람은 '이인자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means the most outstanding person in a field, similar to '최고' or '1등' but used only for people. It can also point to the top person in an organization, and the one just below is called '이인자'.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 일조량이 많아서 과일이 달아요.
examples.en: This area gets a lot of sunshine, so the fruit is sweet.
In winter there's little sunshine, so my mood sinks.

examples.ko: 일조량이 부족하면 식물이 잘 자라지 않아요.
examples.en: If there isn't enough sunlight, plants don't grow well.
A south-facing house gets plenty of sunlight, so it's warm.
Thanks to the sunshine this year, the farming went well.

examples.ko: 아파트를 고를 때 일조량도 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: When choosing an apartment, check the amount of sunlight too.

explain: '햇빛'이 일상적인 말이라면 '일조량'은 농사, 집 고르기, 날씨 뉴스처럼 햇볕을 양으로 따질 때 써요. '일조량이 많다/적다/부족하다'처럼 말해요. 햇볕이 비치는 시간은 '일조 시간'이라고 해요.
explain_en: While '햇빛' is the everyday word, '일조량' is used when sunshine is measured as an amount, such as in farming, house hunting and weather news. You say '일조량이 많다/적다/부족하다'. The length of time the sun shines is called '일조 시간'.
